payload.goal: Let an initiative be closed. Closing records a terminal status (done or dropped, with a reason) and unbinds every branch pointing at it — and session-first resolution across the statusline and hooks is what makes that safe: the session that closed it keeps its record until it ends, while a new session on the unbound branch is told to start or switch instead of landing on finished work.

payload.because: A binding that outlives the work it points at is how a fresh session ends up oriented on something already finished — the concrete symptom the user hit: a new session's statusline reading `auto-update 11/11`. Unbinding makes the branch honestly say "nothing here" instead. Session-first resolution is what makes unbinding safe rather than destructive: verified that with the branch unbound today, the statusline's record segment vanishes entirely and the PostToolUse hook exits 0 while silently dropping the event, so the rest of the session would go dark. The write path already resolves session-before-branch (context.ts:285) — extending that precedence to the read surfaces makes closing a clean boundary at the SESSION edge rather than a mid-session cliff, and is strictly better behavior even for records that are never closed.
payload.chose: Closing an initiative UNBINDS every branch pointing at it (user ruling, 2026-08-05). Reopening happens by binding again, which is a new-session act. The current session is not disrupted: its statusline keeps showing the closed record and its hooks keep routing, because every surface resolves SESSION FIRST and branch binding second.
payload.over: (a) Warn but never touch the binding — closing stays a record fact and the branch keeps pointing at finished work, so a fresh session still lands on it and must switch by hand. (b) Infer closure from all-phases-resolved and add no state — cannot tell "finished" from "abandoned at 3/10", cannot express "closed, but 4.1 was never built", and records no when or why.

tasks.title: Back-compat probe, the task-drop-state 1.1 discipline: verify EMPIRICALLY against published 0.18.x what an older engine does with (a) an `initiative_status_changed` event it does not know, and (b) a bindings.json whose entry was removed. Expected: unknown event type skipped with a warning, and an unbound branch read as unbound — both degrading safe. Confirm or refute before designing on top of it.

DECIDE the cross-process session→initiative mechanism, the crux of the whole initiative. The pin is in-memory per MCP server process (context.ts:51), so a statusline or hook process cannot read it. Options: scan each initiative log with the existing registeredAt(), or persist the pin (e.g. .sofar/sessions/) for a single cheap read. Weigh statusline cost — it re-renders constantly and `speed` is a standing concern — against stale-pin cleanup. Log a Decision.

Decide what a hook does when NEITHER a session pin nor a branch binding resolves. Today it exits 0 and silently drops the event (verified). Silence respects BD22 (never break the session) but loses telemetry invisibly; lazily binding would recreate misrouting. Pick, and make the choice observable.

INITIATIVE_STATUSES = active|done|dropped and an `initiative_status_changed` event (payload {status, note?}) — schema lives ONLY in packages/schema/src/. Two terminal states, mirroring tasks and phases: `done` = finished, `dropped` = abandoned. No near-synonyms (task-drop-state D1's lesson). `dropped` requires a reason, per task-drop-state D3.

Fold: InitiativeState gains status (default `active` — a log with no such event is unchanged), plus when it closed and the reason. Terminal statuses are resolved; reopening is just another status event, so history stays append-only.

`sofar close [slug]` CLI + MCP tool: append the status event, then remove EVERY bindings.json entry pointing at that slug (not just the current branch — a closed record should have no branch aimed at it). Atomic and idempotent; bindings.json is committed and shared, so a torn write is not acceptable.

Define reopening: what `sofar switch <closed-slug>` does — silently reopen, refuse, or require `--reopen`. The user's rule is that working on it again is what revives it, so the default must not be a dead end; decide and log it.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Session-first resolution (what makes unbinding safe)

tasks.title: Implement 1.2's mechanism so ANY process can answer "which initiative is session X registered in", and make session-before-branch the shared precedence — the read path currently has no pin at all (resolveInitiative), while the write path already does (resolveWriteInitiative, context.ts:285).

Statusline: resolve session-first, branch second; render a closed record distinctly from a live one; render nothing when neither resolves. A drop-free, close-free line must stay byte-identical — the statusline re-renders constantly and its width is the felt surface.

Hooks (PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd) resolve session-first, so closing mid-session stops silently dropping the rest of the session's telemetry. This is a bug fix independent of closing: an unbound branch loses events today with no signal at all.

SessionStart injection: an unbound branch must say so and name the next move (`sofar new` / `sofar switch`) instead of erroring or injecting nothing; a session pinned to a closed record gets it WITH a closed banner, so the agent knows not to queue new work there. Stays inside the ≤10,000-char guarantee.

`sofar next` omits closed initiatives — a closed record has no next action, and today it would still be listed. `sofar list` marks them and sorts them below open ones. `sofar status <slug>` shows the closed status with when and why.

doctor: a closed initiative that still has a branch bound (hand-edits and merges happen), and the mirror of the stale-phase axis — every phase resolved but the initiative never closed. The second is the initiative-level version of the exact false signal task-drop-state fixed one level down.

docs/SPEC.md is authoritative: the new event type, the status set, the InitiativeState fields, the session-before-branch resolution precedence, unbind-on-close semantics, and §Acceptance criteria. No task is done until its criteria pass.

Dogfood the exact case that prompted this: close repo-memory-capture and task-drop-state, then confirm THIS session's statusline still shows its record while a genuinely fresh session on the unbound branch is told to start or switch. Also confirm closing does not silence the closing session's own hooks.

payload.text:
Scoping evidence, measured 2026-08-05 on published 0.18.0 in a scratch repo — the two facts D1 rests on, so Phase 3 is a bug fix and not only a feature:

With the branch unbound (bindings.json emptied):
1. STATUSLINE — the record segment vanishes entirely. Not degraded, absent. `sofar statusline` is a fresh process per render and resolves via resolveInitiative (the READ path, which has no session pin), so there is nothing to fall back to.
2. POSTTOOLUSE HOOK — exits 0 and writes nothing. The event is silently dropped: no warning, no fallback, no trace. A session that closed its initiative would go dark for its remaining telemetry.

Why the pin cannot help today: ActiveSession lives in a SessionBox that is in-memory per MCP server process (context.ts:51 — "one in-memory active session per server process"). A statusline or hook process literally cannot read it. But the statusline DOES receive session_id in its hook JSON, and registeredAt(logPath, sessionId) (context.ts:94) already answers "was this session registered in this log" — so the mechanism exists, it just has never been wired to the read surfaces. That is 1.2's decision: scan-with-registeredAt vs persist-the-pin.

Scope correction, so nobody inherits an overclaim: session-first resolution does NOT fix the misrouting failure recorded as repo-memory-capture M3. Session a18d80d0 was registered under the branch binding by the SessionStart hook, so resolving session-first would keep honoring that same wrong registration. What this initiative DOES fix is the specific harm that followed: a CLOSED initiative kept absorbing a foreign session's commands. Once closing unbinds, a finished record can no longer be the default destination for whatever else happens in the checkout.

1.1 back-compat probe — EMPIRICAL, published sofar.sh@0.18.0 in an isolated npm install against a throwaway repo (scratch: probe/). Nothing refuted; one refinement.

(a) Unknown `initiative_status_changed` event (well-formed envelope, future type): CONFIRMED degrade-safe. Fold emits `line 2: unknown event type "initiative_status_changed" — skipped`; exit 0 on status/list/next/statusline; doctor reports it under Record health as WARN and still ends "no problems found, 1 warning". Replay CONTINUES past it — a note_added appended after the unknown line applied normally. The line survives verbatim through a subsequent old-engine WRITE (`sofar remember`): log grew by append only, unknown line still present, never rewritten.

(b) Removed bindings.json entry (simulating what `sofar close` will do): CONFIRMED, with the surfaces split three ways.
  - Silent: all FIVE hooks (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end) exit 0 with zero stdout, zero stderr, and append zero events. Includes Stop — so on an unbound branch the write-back guard silently stops guarding.
  - Loud: `sofar status` / `sofar remember` with no slug exit 1; every MCP tool returns isError `unknown_initiative` — including `sofar_start_session` itself. Message says "pass `initiative` explicitly or bind the branch"; it does NOT name `sofar new` / `sofar switch` (4.1's gap).
  - Degraded-but-fine: `list` / `next` render the initiative tagged `[unbound]` and still list it (4.2's premise confirmed). Statusline does not go blank — it drops the sofar segment and renders `repo · main` (42 bytes), exit 0, no stderr.

(c) Unplanned but load-bearing findings:
  - NO lazy re-binding anywhere. After every read path, all five hooks, and both failed writes, bindings.json stayed `{}`. Only `new` and `switch` write it. An old engine therefore cannot silently undo a close.
  - `sofar_start_session {initiative, session_id}` SUCCEEDS on an unbound branch, and subsequent writes route through the in-memory pin without recreating a binding. Session-before-branch precedence already works end-to-end for the MCP write path — in-process only, which is exactly the gap 1.2 has to close for statusline/hooks.

1.1 addendum — the plan's premise for Phase 3 was too pessimistic; measured correction.

`cli/event.ts:201 resolveBound()` ALREADY resolves session-first for every hook, via `homeInitiative()` (context.ts:140) — a cross-process, log-derived scan shipped by record-integrity 1.2/D1. Re-probed 0.18.0 with a REGISTERED session on a fully unbound branch: post-tool-use appended `file_touched` to the right initiative, and session-start injected the full 740-byte record block. So hooks already survive unbinding.

The earlier "unbound branch silently drops hook events" measurement holds only for an UNREGISTERED session (no `session_started` in any log) — homeInitiative returns null, branch returns null, hook exits 0 silently. That is 1.3's actual case, and it should be restated that way: the drop condition is "no pin AND no binding", not "no binding".

Statusline is the real gap: `recordSegment` (statusline.ts:179) calls `ctx.resolveInitiative()` — branch only. statusline.ts never reads `session_id` at all, though the harness passes it. So 3.2 is the load-bearing change; 3.3 shrinks to a verification task plus whatever 1.3 decides.

Cost measurements on the real 22-initiative, 2.8 MB record (inputs for 1.2):
  statusline end-to-end today: ~55 ms (node startup + fold dominate)
  homeInitiative HIT (branch-bound preferred log, 1 read): 0.07 ms → +0.1%
  homeInitiative MISS (full scan, all 22 logs): 2.9 ms → +5%, and only on the unbound/re-homed path closing creates

payload.because: Measured on the real 22-initiative, 2.8 MB record: the statusline costs ~55 ms end-to-end today (node startup + fold dominate), and homeInitiative adds 0.07 ms on the hit path (+0.1%, invisible) and 2.9 ms on a full-scan miss (+5%) — and the miss only occurs on the unbound/re-homed path that closing creates. The cost that worried this task is not there. A persisted pin would be a second store that can desync from the truth log, which record-integrity D1 already ruled against, and would need stale-pin cleanup the scan does not. Decisive: the mechanism is already proven in production — hooks route correctly on a fully unbound branch today (measured against published 0.18.0), so this reuses a shipped, tested path instead of introducing a parallel one.
payload.chose: Reuse the existing log-derived homeInitiative() scan as the cross-process session→initiative mechanism, and share event.ts's resolveBound precedence (branch computed as the PREFERRED candidate, session home wins, branch as fallback) across statusline and hooks
payload.over: Persisting the pin to a second store (e.g. .sofar/sessions/<id>) for a single cheap read

payload.note: Probed published 0.18.0 in an isolated install. Both halves confirmed degrade-safe — unknown initiative_status_changed skipped with a warning (replay continues past it, log never rewritten), removed binding degrades rather than corrupts. Nothing refuted. Two unplanned findings changed the plan: no old-engine path ever re-creates a binding (only new/switch write bindings.json, so a close cannot be silently undone), and hooks ALREADY resolve session-first via homeInitiative, so they survive unbinding today.

Decided: reuse homeInitiative()'s log-derived scan, no persisted pin. See the decision — the statusline cost that framed this task was measured and is 0.1% on the hit path, 5% on the miss path, against a ~55 ms baseline.

Hooks are drivable by piping their JSON payload into `.claude/hooks/<name>.sh`. This is how task-drop-state 1.1 and initiative-lifecycle 1.1 were verified; a working-tree test cannot answer what an OLDER engine does with a NEWER log.

payload.because: The drop is per-event but the condition is per-session — "this session is registered nowhere and the branch is unbound" is ONE fact, so it belongs once where the agent reads, not N times where nothing does. (i) is disqualified twice over: it recreates the misrouting record-integrity 1.2/D1 fixed, and it would let a hook silently undo a close — 1.1 measured that no engine path re-creates a binding today (only new/switch write bindings.json), and that property is what makes close-unbinds safe. (ii) fires on every tool use, so the noise scales with work, and BD22 says never break the session. (iii) is a second store outside the truth log, which record-integrity D1 rules against — the same reason 1.2 rejected a persisted pin. Measured today: on an unbound branch with an unregistered session, SessionStart injects 0 bytes and the statusline renders `repo · main` — both silently indistinguishable from a healthy repo, which is the actual defect.
payload.chose: When neither a session pin nor a branch binding resolves, hooks keep dropping the event silently (exit 0, never lazily bind) — but the CONDITION becomes observable once per session at the two orienting surfaces that already run: SessionStart injects an unbound notice naming `sofar new` / `sofar switch` (4.1), and the statusline renders an explicit unbound marker instead of merely omitting the record segment (3.2)
payload.over: (i) lazily binding the branch at hook time; (ii) warning on stderr per dropped event; (iii) recording drops to a sidecar file outside the event log

payload.note: Decided: keep the silent per-event drop, never lazily bind; surface the condition once per session via SessionStart (4.1) and the statusline unbound marker (3.2). Restates the premise 1.1 corrected — the drop condition is "no pin AND no binding", not "no binding".

payload.because: The user's rule is that working on it again is what revives it, and `switch` IS that act — it means "this branch works on this now", which a closed record cannot honour while staying closed. Refusing makes closing a dead end, which the rule forbids. A --reopen flag only adds a step to a decision the user already expressed by typing switch; the flag would be discoverable solely by hitting the refusal it exists to bypass. Reading a closed record needs no binding (`sofar status <slug>` already does that), so switch is never the accidental path. The event keeps the revival auditable — the log shows closed-then-reopened rather than an unexplained return to active, which is what append-only history is for.

  repo has NO record at all               → no segment, exactly as today (most repos, including every non-sofar one)
